In Islam, **procrastination** (especially when it leads to unnecessary stress, poor work, or disrespect for others) is generally discouraged for several reasons: 1. **Wasting Time** – Time is a precious gift from Allah (ﷺ), and wasting it without necessity is considered a sin (*fisq*). The Prophet (ﷺ) said: > *"The world is better for you and more beloved to you than it was before, and your deeds have been recorded. So whoever does good will see it, and whoever does evil will see it."* (Sahih Muslim) Procrastinating without a valid reason may be seen as wasting time that could have been used for productive, beneficial, or worship-related activities. 2. **Reliance on Allah (Tawakkul)** – Islam encourages trust in Allah’s plan but also emphasizes responsibility (*amr bil ma’ruf*). Waiting until the last minute without effort may be seen as a lack of diligence, which contradicts the principle of working hard (*ijtihad*) while relying on Allah. 3. **Respect for Commitments** – If the project was assigned by a teacher, employer, or authority figure, delaying it without a valid reason may be seen as disrespectful or irresponsible. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: > *"The strong man is not the one who overcomes others with his strength, but the strong man is the one who controls himself when angry."* (Sahih Bukhari) Procrastination can stem from laziness or lack of self-discipline, which are traits to avoid. 4. **Potential Negative Consequences** – If the boy’s procrastination leads to poor work, missed opportunities, or stress, it may have unintended negative effects on his academic, professional, or spiritual life. ### **Is it Wrong?** - **Yes, if it is habitual, irresponsible, or leads to harm** (e.g., poor grades, missed deadlines, unnecessary stress). - **Less wrong if it’s a one-time oversight** (e.g., unexpected circumstances), but even then, it’s better to plan ahead. ### **What Should Be Done?** - **Repent (Tawbah)** – If the boy realizes his mistake, he should seek forgiveness from Allah and improve. - **Develop Discipline** – Islam encourages self-control (*zuhd*) and productivity (*ijtihad*). - **Plan Ahead** – The Prophet (ﷺ) advised: > *"Make plans for your affairs, but depend on Allah."* (Sunan Ibn Majah) This means balancing preparation with trust in Allah. Would you like guidance on how to improve time management in an Islamic context?
